question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cosecant Function
question.worked_solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x-5csc⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}-5(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}+5csc⁡xcot⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\pi }{2})}+5csc⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})cot⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }+5\cdot 1\cdot 0 \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cotangent Function
question.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{x}^{4}cot⁡x) \\  & =(-8{x}^{3})(cot⁡x)+(-2{x}^{4})(-{csc}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =-8{x}^{3}cot⁡x+2{x}^{4}{csc}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Slope of the Tangent at a Point of a Function Involving Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions
question.problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ if $f(x)=ln⁡x+3csc⁡x.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x+3csc⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}+3(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}-3csc⁡xcot⁡x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\pi }{3})}-3csc⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})cot⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }-3(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}})(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }-3(\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }-2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ if $f(x)=-{x}^{2}+5csc⁡x.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{d}{dx}(-{x}^{2}+5csc⁡x) \\  & =2\cdot (-x)+5(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & =-2x-5csc⁡xcot⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ into the derivative and get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-2(\frac{\pi }{6})-5csc⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})cot⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}-5\cdot 2\cdot \sqrt{3} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}-10\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$
